title: Down the Rabbit Hole: Detecting Online Extremism, Radicalisation, and Politicised Hate Speech
measurement_description: The paper evaluates the focus of existing academic research (from 2015-2021) on detecting extremism, radicalisation, and hate speech, specifically measuring the ideological and geographic biases within this research. A key measurement is the disproportionate focus on Islamic extremism, which the paper identifies as an 'Islamophobic trend in academia'.
findings: The paper identifies a significant bias in academic research towards studying Islamic extremism, which it terms an 'Islamophobic trend'. It found that 77% of US-originating extremism studies targeted Islamic extremism, and it was a global trend in 20% of all studies reviewed. This focus persists despite far-right extremism being a more prevalent domestic threat in Western countries like the US. The paper recommends decoupling religious contexts from political ideologies, for instance, using technical terms like 'radical Islamic extremism' or 'terror-supporting martyrdom' instead of broader religious categories to avoid mischaracterization.
